title: Buffered SSE window coordinator and deterministic call serializer
author: Priya Desai
release_notes: Stabilize SSE streaming by introducing a packetizer/window coordinator and deterministic call serializer to prevent partial-JSON emissions and function-call reordering on reconnect/replay.
description: Background: customers saw rare but high-impact cases where SSE fragment coalescing and transport-level reordering produced truncated JSON frames or out-of-order tool/function call events during reconnects and HTTP/2 headroom shifts. This PR introduces a buffered packetizer + window coordinator inside the streaming stack plus a deterministic call serializer (call-seq) and idempotency token handshake so clients and the OpenAI-compat layer can reliably resume and preserve fncall ordering. Motivation: reduce broken/partial JSON emissions, minimize application-level compensating logic, and make reconnect/replay deterministic. Implementation summary: 1) packetizer: aggregates incoming runtime tokens into bounded windows (configurable via env/route param) and emits well-formed SSE events only at window boundaries or when explicit epoch markers appear; 2) window coordinator: assigns a monotonically increasing window_id + window_checksum and exposes an optional checkpoint token (sse-checkpoint) that clients may ACK — used only for resume heuristics; 3) deterministic call serializer: when an event contains a tool/function call, serializer attaches call_meta: {call_seq, call_idempotency_token}. Calls are emitted in strict call_seq order and the OpenAI-compat adapter preserves call_seq across model fallbacks; 4) reconnect/resume behavior: on reconnect with a checkpoint, server attempts a fast-resume by replaying buffered windows from the last ACKed checkpoint. If checkpoint mismatch, server falls back to re-stream-from-start + explicit resync hint. 5) compatibility shim: openai-compat now maps call_meta to OpenAI-style function_call sentinel plus an embedded __call_seq to avoid breaking older clients. Tests & metrics: added deterministic replay unit tests, end-to-end integration that fuzzes HTTP/2 coalescing, and a perf microbenchmark to ensure added buffering does not regress 99th percentile latency in common short-response workloads. Rollout: feature guarded by route flag streaming.packetizer.enabled (default off). Progressive rollout: beta to select tenants for 48 hours, then broader ramp if no regressions. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged when feature is disabled. See changed files for implementation details.

review_comments: Maya Chen (review): Can we make the default packet window conservative for now (e.g., 16KB or 50ms) to avoid latency regressions on short responses? Also please add metrics for dropped partial-json events.
Priya Desai (author): Updated default to 16KB / 50ms and added metrics sse.packetizer.window_bytes and sse.packetizer.window_duration_ms. Added test that asserts no regressions for sub-1KB responses.

Ethan Li (review): Lgtm overall. A few nits: rename call_seq to __call_seq for the OpenAI shim only; ensure we don't leak internal window_id into public headers. Also please add a safety timeout to avoid indefinitely buffering a stalled connection.
Priya Desai (author): Addressed all nits: OpenAI shim uses __call_seq; window_id now only appears in internal logs and checkpoint tokens (opaque). Added 2s safety flush timeout configurable by route.
Rohan Kapoor (approval): Verified deterministic replay tests locally and ran the http2 fuzz harness. Approving pending CI green.

notes: Feature gated; must enable streaming.packetizer.enabled per-route before traffic. Observability: new metrics and logs added; dashboards updated under Redwood Console > Streaming > Packetizer.
manual_steps:
1) set route flag "streaming.packetizer.enabled=true"
2) monitor sse.packetizer.window_bytes and sse.packetizer.buffered_windows metric
3) if partial JSON regressions occur, set streaming.packetizer.enabled=false and file ENG ticket.
post_merge_actions: Added follow-up ENG-5239 to audit client SDK behavior and roll-forward a user-facing migration note in the SDK changelogs. Scheduled canary rollout for Nov 10 2025.
